item.content:encoded:
The Colorado Rockies are 57–99.
Purple Row After Dark: If the Rockies could steal one player
An absurd rule for absurd times: if the worst team in baseball could steal one player from a playoff club, who should the Rockies take?
One more loss will give them their fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they are almost certainly going to finish with the worst record in baseball.
These are absurd times for the Rockies, so I have devised an appropriately absurd rule to help them out.
The team with the worst record in baseball gets to steal one player from a playoff team.
There are, naturally, some restrictions. We’re freezing the playoff field as it stood before games on Sunday, September 20. The player has to come from one of those 12 teams, cannot be a pending free agent, and you cannot take the player who leads his team in FanGraphs WAR. The Rockies also inherit the player’s existing contract.
No, one player is not suddenly turning the Rockies into a contender. But could one poached superstar at least keep this thing from becoming five consecutive 100-loss seasons?
Here’s the board:
| Team | Off limits: fWAR leader | Highest available fWAR | Other players worth considering |
| Rays | Junior Caminero (5.2) | Drew Rasmussen (4.7) | Jonathan Aranda (3) |
| Guardians | Parker Messick (4.6) | Steven Kwan (3.4) | Gavin Williams (3.4), Brayan Rocchio (3.3), José Ramírez (2.2) |
| Rangers | Ezequiel Duran (4.6) | Jacob deGrom (4.2) | Josh Jung (2.9), Wyatt Langford (2.8) |
| Yankees | Cam Schlittler (6.1) | Ben Rice (4) | Cody Bellinger (3.9), Aaron Judge (2) |
| Red Sox | Willson Contreras (4.1) | Payton Tolle (4) | Ceddanne Rafaela (3.9), Ranger Suárez (3.7) |
| White Sox | Miguel Vargas (5) | Chase Meidroth (4) | Tristan Peters (3.9), Sean Burke (3.1) |
| Brewers | Jacob Misiorowski (6.3) | Brice Turang (5.4) | Jackson Chourio (4), Jake Bauers (3.6) |
| Dodgers | Shohei Ohtani (6.7) | Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.7) | Max Muncy (4.3), Andy Pages (3.9) |
| Braves | Chris Sale (5.7) | Michael Harris II (4) | Matt Olson (4), Drake Baldwin (3.1) |
| Cubs | Pete Crow-Armstrong (10.2) | Alex Bregman (5) | Dansby Swanson (3.6) |
| Padres | Fernando Tatis Jr. (5) | Jackson Merrill (4) | Ty France (3.8), Mason Miller (3.7) |
| Phillies | Cristopher Sánchez (5.8) | Jesús Luzardo (5.6) | Zack Wheeler (3.5), Bryce Harper (3.4) |
For me, the choice comes down to Brice Turang, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Aaron Judge.
Turang is probably the sensible choice.
At 5.4 fWAR, he would easily lead the Rockies, giving them a legitimate top-end player while immediately solving second base for the foreseeable future. He’s 26, hitting .266/.367/.441 with an .808 OPS, and brings value on both sides of the ball with elite range, strong baserunning and a 95th-percentile walk rate.
It would be a very easy way to make the roster better.
But the Rockies really need starting pitching.
Enter Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He’s 14–8 with a 2.51 ERA, 178 strikeouts and a 0.87 WHIP over 179 innings. His Statcast profile is just as impressive: 100th-percentile pitching run value, 99th-percentile fastball run value, 95th-percentile offspeed run value and a 91st-percentile xERA.
Pitchers are risky, and Yamamoto comes with a lot of money attached. But it’s hard to argue with either the profile or the results, and the addition of the Penner family makes absorbing that contract a lot easier to imagine.
Speaking of high-priced items...
Aaron Judge.
Judge being available is basically a loophole created by our own stupid rule. Injuries have limited him to just 285 plate appearances, which is why he sits at only 2 fWAR, but he’s still hitting .241/.360/.511 with 15 home runs.
And the underlying numbers are still very much Judge: a .396 xwOBA, .569 xSLG, 94.0 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5% hard-hit rate.
It is very hard to look at that and say, “No thanks.”
After all, Aaron Judge is the type of hitter that, if he were playing 81 games a year at Coors Field, I might take out a small loan for season tickets.
So who are you stealing?

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we’ll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who’s finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he’ll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn’t totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He’s always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn’t have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We’ve seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who’ll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night’s hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.
How to watch
Location: Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ
First pitch: 4:10 pm E.T.
TV broadcast: YES, DBACKS.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), ESPN 620 AM, La Campesina 101.9 FM & 860 AM (AZ)
Online stream: MLB.tv (out-of-market only), Gotham Sports App

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees lost the second game against the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 5-3. The fact that the loss came on the heels of Aaron Boone keeping Yankees fans concerned about Aaron Judge ahead of the MLB Postseason didn’t help. The fact that it widened the Tampa Bay Rays‘ lead over the Pinstripers for first place in the AL East wasn’t great, either. Still, Cody Bellinger believes in his team.
Apparently, not enough to be convinced that the Yankees may still make it a pennant race with the Rays and come away on top, but he sure is confident that once the postseason arrives, the Bronx Bombers can turn it up a notch. And who knows? Why not win the World Series?
It’s happened before, and the Yankees have already received a good omen from the New York Giants and New York Jets. The signs may be out there. In case they aren’t clear enough, Bellinger’s latest statement might help out even more. The Rays, and frankly, the entire MLB landscape, have been put on notice.
“Yeah, I mean, [the Rays] are playing tremendous baseball. It’s tough to climb up in the standings if they keep winning. Mathematically pretty tough, we have got to keep on rolling,” Bellinger said postgame, via YES Network. “Obviously, the goal is win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days, that’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”
Decisive Rays-Yankees series
Although Bellinger’s admission after the defeat in Phoenix sounded almost like the Yankees were waving the white flag in the pennant race against the Rays, there is still some baseball left to play, and a couple of very meaningful games on the horizon. New York and Tampa Bay will meet for a four-game series at Yankee Stadium (Sept. 22-24, with a doubleheader on Sept. 22) that could very well decide who wins the American League East division.
If the Boston Red Sox can get a win in the rubber match against the Rays while the Yankees secure the series against the D-Backs, then a sweep by New York against Tampa Bay would put both teams at even-Stevens. A sweep is the only way for the Yankees to get the tiebreaker over the Rays, as they are currently down 3-6 in the season’s head-to-head.
Another Rays win over the Pinstripers will clinch the tiebreaker for them. It’s a tough ask for New York, but not impossible. Obviously, without Judge, the climb is only steeper, but it may be perfect timing for a new miracle in the Bronx.

| One game vs | Arizona D-Backs | Boston Red Sox |

item.content:encoded:
On Friday, the New York Yankees announced they will place star outfielder Aaron Judge on the 10-day injured list on Saturday with a right calf strain.
From Bryan Hoch on MLB.com: Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list tomorrow with a right calf strain, the Yankees say. A corresponding move will be made at that time.
According to Jon Heyman of the New York Post, Judge will be eligible to return for the final game of the regular season.
The Yankees removed Judge from Wednesday’s loss to the Minnesota Twins at Target Field in the sixth inning due to his calf injury.
“I tried to play it off and see how long we can go because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said. “Talking it over I thought it’d be the right move to come out so we don’t cost the team on the field or cost the team on the basepaths.” Before the Yankees’ game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix on Friday, Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger was asked about Judge’s injury.
New York Yankees Star Cody Bellinger Makes Statement on Aaron Judge’s Injury
“Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he’s the best hitter in the game,” Bellinger said to Hoch. “For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody.”
Aaron Judge has missed most of the season with a right rib stress fracture. New York placed him on the IL on June 2. He didn’t return until Sept. 7.
Since making his MLB debut in 2016, Judge has slashed 291/.410/.610 with 386 home runs and 871 RBI. He has won three AL MVP Awards.
New York Yankees Right Now
The Yankees began a three-game series against the Diamondbacks in Arizona on Friday night.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are out West on Friday night to begin a weekend series with the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Ahead of the matchup, New York received some bad news as superstar Aaron Judge heads back to the IL with a calf strain. Yankees manager Aaron Boone also made a few notable changes to his starting lineup for the series opener.
Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision
After spending pretty much the entire season in a platoon role and not starting the last time the Yankees played on Wednesday, veteran slugger Paul Goldschmidt is in the lineup Friday, starting at first base and batting leadoff.
He’ll bat in front of Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Ben Rice, who will move into the cleanup spot.
Here’s the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/18 P. Goldschmidt 1B C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF B. Rice DH A. Rosario 3B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B G. Cole SP.”
Yankees 9/18
P. Goldschmidt 1B
C. Bellinger LF
H. Ramos RF
B. Rice DH
A. Rosario 3B
S. Jones CF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
G. Cole SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 18, 2026
Goldschmidt’s 2026 Season
In his 16th MLB season and his second as a member of the Yankees, Goldschmidt has appeared in 101 games for New York, and across 332 at-bats, he’s hitting .253 with 42 runs, 84 hits, 18 home runs, and 50 RBIs while slugging .458 and maintaining a .773 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Friday’s contest with the D-backs holding an 88-64 overall record. They sit 5.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East division lead and the No. 1 overall seed in the American League.
Currently, the Yankees hold the top Wild Card spot, and if the season ended today, they’d host a best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx against, coincidentally enough, the Boston Red Sox in what would mark a rematch of the 2025 postseason.
